title: Hello, my name is Ani
title_target: မင်္ဂလာပါ၊ ကျွန်မနာမည် အာနီပါ — miⁿ-ga-la-ba, cha.ma. na-mè a-nee ba
goal: Greet people, say your name, ask how someone is, and choose the right word for "I" — because in Burmese that word depends on whether the speaker is a man or a woman.
bekal: greet people with မင်္ဂလာပါ and greet them back
say your name with …နာမည် … ပါ
choose between ကျွန်တော် and ကျွန်မ without hesitating
ask and answer "how are you?" with နေကောင်းလား
say yes and no with ဟုတ်ကဲ့ and မဟုတ်ဘူး

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — Outside a house in Yangon
dialogs.intro: Ani has just arrived in Yangon to work for a year. Min Aung, the next-door neighbor, greets her at the gate. Notice one thing from the very first line: Min Aung calls himself ကျွန်တော်, while Ani calls herself ကျွန်မ — and both mean "I".

lines.text: [မင်္ဂလာပါ|miⁿ-ga-la-ba]။ [ကျွန်တော့်|cha.nò.] [နာမည်|na-mè] [မင်းအောင်|miⁿ:-owⁿ] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: Hello. My name is Min Aung.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [မင်္ဂလာပါ|miⁿ-ga-la-ba]။ [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [နာမည်|na-mè] [အာနီ|a-nee] [ပါ|ba]။

lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [ဂျာကာတာ|ja-ka-ta] [က|ga.] [ပါ|ba]။

lines.text: [နေ|nay] [ကောင်း|kowⁿ:] [လား|la:]။

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [နေကောင်းပါတယ်|nay-kowⁿ:-ba-dè]။ [ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်|chay:-zoo:-tiⁿ-ba-dè]။ [မင်းအောင်|miⁿ:-owⁿ] [ရော|yò:]။
lines.id: I'm fine, thank you. And you, Min Aung?

lines.speaker: မင်းအောင်:
lines.text: [ကျွန်တော်|cha.nò] [လည်း|lè:] [နေကောင်းပါတယ်|nay-kowⁿ:-ba-dè]။ [မြန်မာစကား|myaⁿ-ma-za.ga:] [ပြော|pyò:] [တတ်|tak] [လား|la:]။
lines.id: I'm fine too. Can you speak Burmese?

lines.text: [နည်းနည်း|nè:-nè:] [ပါ|ba]။ [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [သင်|thiⁿ] [နေ|nay] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။

lines.text: [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [လည်း|lè:] [ဝမ်းသာပါတယ်|waⁿ:-tha-ba-dè]။ [ဒီမှာ|dee-hma] [နေ|nay] [လား|la:]။
lines.id: Nice to meet you too. Do you live here?
lines.literal: I(f) — also — glad-polite-statement. here-at — live — Q?

lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [ဒီမှာ|dee-hma] [နေပါတယ်|nay-ba-dè]။ [ဝင်|wiⁿ] [ပါ|ba]၊ [လက်ဖက်ရည်|la.hpèk-yay] [သောက်|thowk] [ရအောင်|ya.-owⁿ]။
lines.id: Yes, we live here. Come in, let's have some tea.

grammars.title: ⚠️ ကျွန်တော် vs ကျွန်မ — "I" depends on the SPEAKER'S gender
body: English uses one word, "I", for everyone. Burmese doesn't. The word you choose depends on **who is speaking**, not on who you're speaking to — and that choice never changes for the rest of the conversation.

head: Speaker
Word
Say it
Possessive form
rows: ကျွန်တော့် — *cha.nò.*
ကျွန်တော်တို့ — *cha.nò-doh.*

after: The **possessive** is made by switching the last syllable to the creaky tone — shown by the dot under တော့်. ကျွန်တော် (I) → ကျွန်တော့် (my). ကျွန်မ doesn't change at all, because its tone is already creaky.

⚠️ ငါ is only for close friends, younger siblings, or children. Using it with someone you've just met sounds rude — far ruder than a casual "yo" in English. For your whole first year, use ကျွန်တော်/ကျွန်မ with everyone and you'll never get it wrong.

grammars.title: ပါ — one syllable that changes your whole tone
body: ပါ (*ba*) has no meaning of its own. It's a politeness particle, and it's what separates a courteous sentence from one that sounds cold. It can go almost anywhere: after a name, after a verb, after a command.

head: Without ပါ
With ပါ
The difference
rows: နေကောင်းတယ် — *nay-kowⁿ:-dè*
နေကောင်းပါတယ် — *nay-kowⁿ:-ba-dè*

after: It's pronounced *ba*, not *pa*, because it leans on the word before it. This p → b change happens all over Burmese and you'll meet it constantly; this book always writes the sound you **actually hear**, not the letter on the page.

grammars.title: Greetings and goodbyes
body: မင်္ဂလာပါ comes from the Pali word *maṅgala*, "blessing" — related to the Sanskrit *mangala* you may know from yoga or Buddhist chants. Use it any time, morning to night.

head: Burmese
Say it
English
rows: နေကောင်းပါတယ်
ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်
တောင်းပန်ပါတယ်

after: ⚠️ နေကောင်းလား literally means "live — well — Q?", so the answer uses the verb too: နေကောင်းပါတယ်, not just "well". Answering with a single word sounds like you're cutting the conversation short.

grammars.title: …လား and answering yes or no
body: Asking a question in Burmese doesn't require flipping anything around. Just put **လား** (*la:*) at the end of the sentence, and a statement becomes a yes-or-no question.

head: Sentence
Say it
Meaning
rows: မြန်မာစကား ပြောတတ်တယ်
မြန်မာစကား ပြောတတ်လား

after: ⚠️ Burmese negation uses **two** parts at once: **မ** before the verb and **ဘူး** after it. မဟုတ်ဘူး = မ + ဟုတ် + ဘူး. Forgetting one of them is the number-one beginner mistake, and you'll meet this pattern in every unit from here on.

blocks.text: These four sentences are enough for an entire first introduction. Learn them as one block, then swap in your own details. The lines use the male form; women simply swap ကျွန်တော် for ကျွန်မ.

head: English
Burmese
Say it
rows: မင်္ဂလာပါ။
ကျွန်တော့်နာမည် ဗူဒီ ပါ။
မြန်မာစကား သင်နေပါတယ်။
တွေ့ရတာ ဝမ်းသာပါတယ်။

blocks.title: Two things that make you sound natural right away
items: **Use the other person's name, not "you".** People in Myanmar say "Would Ani like some tea?" rather than "Would you like some tea?". Using the name sounds warm; using a pronoun sounds distant.

**Add ရော (*yò:*) to bounce a question back.** After answering how you are, just say the other person's name followed by ရော — မင်းအောင်ရော။ It's the same as "and you?" and saves you a whole sentence.

Put the words in the right order. Remember: the verb and its ending go at the end.

ပါ / က / အင်ဒိုနီးရှား / ကျွန်မ
